A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete 21-page and 23-page contents, including equations, figures, references, and appendices, support reliable comparison and matching of relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian simulations and representation analyses of translated sentences, ImageNet image pairs, and Flickr30k image-caption pairs, including supplementary controls.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical analyses and adds smaller-Llama and multilingual-BERT comparisons, BERT token-asymmetry results, and synthetic comparisons with CKA.

M1.justification: As written, the II estimator changes nearest-neighbor rank from 0 in v2 Equation 1 to 1 in v4 Section 2 while retaining the normalization, introducing a small finite-sample offset. Token concatenation, sign binarization, and Hamming-distance analysis remain unchanged; a corresponding implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: The OPUS Books languages, ImageNet same-class image task, and Flickr30k image-caption coverage remain unchanged. v4 adds a noisy, rank-controlled Gaussian mapping scenario beyond the earlier shared-component simulation. Additional neural models do not constitute new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Figure 2a extends the DeepSeek-V3/Llama3.1-8B comparison with Llama3.2-1B, Llama3.2-3B, and multilingual BERT. Figure 1 newly evaluates CKA against II in synthetic comparisons. Neighborhood-overlap and CLIP comparisons were already present in v2.

E3.justification: v4 introduces rank-1-to-10 noisy Gaussian transformations, comparisons at 1,000 and 100,000 dimensions, additional model configurations, and a 7,500-sentence BERT asymmetry analysis. The BID experiment's stated sentence-length filter changes from 40–50 tokens in v2 Appendix I to 40–80 in v4 Appendix H, despite retaining the plot; a rerun is not established.

E4.justification: The Gaussian analysis expands from binary-versus-real calibration to testing directional predictability and CKA's high-dimensional discrimination. v4 Appendix J adds a non-autoregressive BERT control for token asymmetry. The multilingual DeepSeek asymmetry analysis is relocated, while existing pooling, shuffling, and real-activation binarization checks remain.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 5 reports ten repetitions with 1-sigma bootstrap bands; the reworked Gaussian experiments in v4 Figure 1 report standard errors over ten jackknife repetitions. Existing language jackknife and image/CLIP bootstrap reporting is largely retained. The PDFs do not establish an increase in repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: v4 adds CKA, smaller-Llama, and BERT results, including BERT's negative central-layer asymmetry. The existing Llama-8B English-Spanish minimum changes from approximately 0.3 in v2 Figure 1a to 0.43 in v4 Figure 2a under the same stated setup, although v4's prose retains 0.3. Most other plots, including CLIP results, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 removes the explicit copula/conditional-mutual-information upper-bound statement from v2 Section 2. Its II definition also changes the rank origin without a compensating normalization adjustment. The BID and token-asymmetry definitions remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract drops explicit DeepSeek-over-Llama superiority and causal token-correlation claims, and the contribution list drops semantic-region growth with model size. The second contribution shifts toward comparing token summaries. Core semantic-layer and cross-modal alignment claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 more explicitly conditions semantic-quality interpretations on alignment and the Platonic hypothesis, and partly attributes DeepSeek's final-layer jump to sparse layer plotting. It adds explicit limitations concerning the limited language-pair sample and specialized cross-lingual retrieval models.

D1.justification: v4 removes v2 Appendix C's origin/destination splitting procedure and guidance to use approximately 200–500 origins, plus DeepSeek's batch size of 30. It adds model identifiers and licenses for the smaller Llamas and BERT, and discloses layer subsampling. Hardware information and the promised code release upon acceptance remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds Chughtai et al. (2023) and Common Crawl language statistics, elaborates its distinction from Wendler et al.'s logit-lens analysis, and removes Wild et al. (2025) with the implementation discussion. The broader positioning around representation alignment and the Platonic hypothesis remains.

P1.justification: Section 2 is substantially rewritten, and the abstract, contributions, and results narrative are reframed. Section 3.1.4 moves into Appendix I, the implementation appendix is removed, other appendices are reorganized, and acknowledgments are added. Citations change from numeric to author-year throughout.

P2.justification: The single appendix Gaussian calibration display is replaced by two-panel main-text Figure 1. The model-comparison plot and legend expand, and BERT asymmetry Figure 11 is added. The former Figure 3 moves to the appendix as Figure 10; most other artwork is reused with revised placement or captions.

improvement.justification: Added model controls, CKA diagnostics, and more cautious interpretations provide useful support. However, v4's revised Llama-8B curve conflicts with its retained 0.3 minimum in Section 3.1 and the retained token-window results, while implementation guidance is removed. These unresolved numerical and reproducibility issues prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
